title: Pop pop pop

clues.t: My inventors were trying to make textured wallpaper in 1957.
Then they tried selling me as greenhouse insulation.
IBM used me to protect its computers, which made me a hit.
I have my own appreciation day in January.
People find popping me very satisfying.
Plastic sheet full of air bubbles for packing.

pearl: Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes made it by sealing two shower curtains together.

title: Six more weeks

clues.t: I’m also called a woodchuck.
I’m a kind of marmot, a big ground squirrel.
I hibernate through winter in a burrow.
On 2 February, crowds in Pennsylvania watch for me.
If I see my shadow, legend says six more weeks of winter.
A Bill Murray film is named after my day.

pearl: Punxsutawney Phil has ‘forecast’ since 1887, with an accuracy roughly like a coin toss.

title: 88 keys

clues.t: I was invented in Italy around 1700 by Bartolomeo Cristofori.
My full name means ‘soft-loud’.
Inside me, felt hammers hit strings.
I usually have 88 keys.
My keys are black and white.
Beethoven, Mozart and Chopin wrote for me.

pearl: Pianoforte was named because, unlike the harpsichord, it could play both soft and loud.

title: Fold it

clues.t: My name comes from Japanese words for ‘fold’ and ‘paper’.
Traditional versions of me use no cuts or glue.
Engineers use my ideas to fold solar panels for space.
Folding 1,000 of my cranes is said to grant a wish.
A single square sheet can become almost anything.
The art of folding paper.

pearl: Sadako Sasaki’s story made the thousand paper cranes a worldwide symbol of peace.

title: Ringed

clues.t: I could float in a giant bath: I’m less dense than water.
My day lasts only about 10.5 hours.
My moon Titan has lakes of liquid methane.
I have the most known moons of any planet.
I’m the sixth planet from the Sun.
My rings are made of ice and rock.

pearl: The rings are huge but very thin: often just tens of metres thick.

title: New Year’s guest

clues.t: I have rectangular pupils.
My babies are called kids.
Coffee was discovered, legend says, when I got jumpy eating berries.
Some of me ‘faint’ when startled, stiffening and falling over.
I can climb steep cliffs and even trees.
2027 is the Year of me in the Chinese zodiac.

pearl: Rectangular pupils give goats a wide panoramic view to watch for predators.

title: Gone for good

clues.t: I lived only on the island of Mauritius.
My closest living relatives are pigeons.
I couldn’t fly and had no fear of people.
I was gone within about 80 years of Dutch sailors arriving.
I appear in Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland.
‘Dead as a …’

pearl: Introduced rats, pigs and monkeys eating eggs probably did more harm than hunting.

title: Bamboo diet

clues.t: I have a ‘thumb’ that’s really an enlarged wrist bone.
I’m a carnivore by family but eat mostly plants.
I eat for up to 14 hours a day.
China has lent me to zoos as a gesture of friendship.
I live in the mountains of central China.
A black-and-white bear that eats bamboo.

pearl: A newborn panda is about 1/900th of its mother’s weight, the size of a stick of butter.

title: Flip it

clues.t: I’m eaten on Shrove Tuesday, before Lent.
In England, people race while tossing me in a frying pan.
A famous race in Olney has run since 1445.
In France I’m thin and called a crêpe.
I’m made from batter of flour, eggs and milk.
Stacked with maple syrup and butter.

pearl: Shrove Tuesday used up rich foods like eggs and butter before the Lent fast.

title: Ice house

clues.t: My name means ‘house’ in Inuktitut.
I’m built in a spiral of snow blocks.
I can be 40 °C warmer inside than out.
My entrance tunnel is lower than the floor to trap warm air.
I’m built from blocks of packed snow.
A dome-shaped snow shelter.

pearl: Snow is full of air pockets, which make it an excellent insulator.

title: Bright idea

clues.t: My inventor’s birthday is 11 February.
Thomas Edison tested thousands of materials for my filament.
Joseph Swan lit a house in England with me first.
A carbonised bamboo filament made me last.
One of me in a US fire station has glowed since 1901.
A cartoon drawing of me means ‘good idea’.

pearl: The ‘Centennial Light’ in Livermore, California, rarely switched off, is over 120 years old.

title: Darwin’s islands

clues.t: My name comes from an old Spanish word for tortoise.
I’m part of Ecuador.
My finches helped inspire a famous theory.
Charles Darwin visited me in 1835, aboard HMS Beagle.
My marine iguanas swim and eat seaweed.
Pacific islands of giant tortoises.

pearl: Darwin’s birthday, 12 February, is celebrated as Darwin Day.

title: Elementary

clues.t: My creator was a doctor: Arthur Conan Doyle.
I was partly based on a surgeon who taught him, Joseph Bell.
I play the violin and keep tobacco in a Persian slipper.
I live at 221B Baker Street.
My friend and narrator is Dr Watson.
Deerstalker hat, magnifying glass, great detective.

pearl: Dr Joseph Bell of Edinburgh could guess a patient’s job from a glance, which inspired the character.

title: Love is in the air

clues.t: I’m related to apples, pears and almonds.
My hips are packed with vitamin C.
There are thousands of varieties of me.
A war in England was named after me.
My stems have prickles, often called thorns.
Red ones of me are given on Valentine’s Day.

pearl: During World War II, Britain collected rose hips to make vitamin C syrup for children.

title: Windy day

clues.t: I was invented in China more than 2,000 years ago.
Benjamin Franklin famously flew me in a thunderstorm.
A bird of prey shares my name.
The Wright brothers tested ideas for their plane with me.
I need wind and a long string.
You fly me at the beach on a windy day.

pearl: Box kites designed by Australian Lawrence Hargrave helped shape early aircraft.

title: Movie snack

clues.t: I’m a special type of corn with a hard, moisture-sealing hull.
Water inside me turns to steam and bursts me open.
Archaeologists found me in a 1,000-year-old Peruvian tomb.
I became a cinema snack during the Great Depression.
I can be sweet, salty or buttery.
You eat me at the movies.

pearl: A kernel pops at about 180 °C, when the pressure inside bursts the hull.

title: Standing on one leg

clues.t: I filter food upside down with my beak.
I’m born grey or white.
My pink colour comes from carotenoids in algae and shrimp.
A group of me is called a flamboyance.
I often stand on one leg, even asleep.
A tall pink wading bird.

pearl: The ‘knee’ that seems to bend backwards is really the flamingo’s ankle.

title: Demoted

clues.t: I was discovered on 18 February 1930.
An 11-year-old English girl suggested my name.
My largest moon, Charon, is about half my size.
New Horizons flew past me in 2015 and found a heart-shaped plain.
In 2006 I was reclassified as a dwarf planet.
I used to be the ninth planet.

pearl: Venetia Burney, 11, suggested the name of the Roman god of the underworld.

title: Bong

clues.t: Strictly, my name belongs to a bell, not a tower.
My tower was renamed after Queen Elizabeth II in 2012.
Pennies on my pendulum adjust my timing.
My bell cracked soon after it was installed.
I stand at the Houses of Parliament.
London’s famous clock tower.

pearl: Adding or removing a single old penny changes the clock by about 0.4 seconds a day.

title: Longships

clues.t: Despite the pictures, our helmets didn’t have horns.
We reached North America about 500 years before Columbus.
Some days of the week are named after our gods.
We came from Scandinavia.
We raided, traded and sailed in longships.
Norse seafarers of about 800 to 1050 AD.

pearl: Thursday is Thor’s day; Wednesday is Odin’s (Woden’s) day.

title: Three scripts

clues.t: French soldiers found me in Egypt in 1799.
The British took me after defeating the French.
I carry the same decree in three scripts.
I helped Jean-François Champollion crack hieroglyphs.
I’m one of the British Museum’s most visited objects.
My name now means a key to understanding something.

pearl: The three scripts are hieroglyphs, Demotic and ancient Greek.

title: Night watch

clues.t: I can turn my head about 270 degrees.
My eyes are tubes, not balls, so they can’t move.
Soft fringes on my feathers make my flight almost silent.
I cough up pellets of fur and bones.
A group of me is called a parliament.
A wise night bird that hoots.

pearl: Barn owls can catch mice in total darkness by sound alone.

title: Carrot nose

clues.t: People have built me since at least the Middle Ages.
Michelangelo was reportedly asked to build me for a Florence ruler.
My eyes are often made of coal.
In a famous film, one of me loves warm hugs.
I’m made of two or three snowballs stacked up.
I have a carrot for a nose.

pearl: In 1494 Piero de’ Medici reportedly had Michelangelo build a snowman in his courtyard.

title: Swing those hips

clues.t: Ancient Egyptian children played with hoops of dried grapevine.
A plastic version of me sold 25 million in 1958.
My name comes from a Hawaiian dance.
The record for spinning lots of me at once is over 200.
You keep me spinning by moving your hips.
A plastic ring you twirl around your waist.

pearl: Wham-O’s plastic hoop became one of the biggest toy crazes ever.

title: Showing off

clues.t: Strictly, only the male of me is a peacock.
My tail feathers can be over 1.5 metres long.
My colours come from tiny structures, not pigment.
I’m the national bird of India.
I shake my tail to make a rustling sound when courting.
A bird with a huge fan of ‘eye’ feathers.

pearl: The shimmering blue is structural colour: light bouncing off tiny crystal-like structures.

title: Nose job

clues.t: My story was first published in Italy in 1883.
My creator, Carlo Collodi, first ended my story with me hanged; readers demanded more.
A cricket gives me advice.
I was carved from wood by Geppetto.
My nose grows when I lie.
A puppet who wants to be a real boy.

pearl: Disney’s 1940 film made the cricket, Jiminy, a star.

title: Ice bear

clues.t: Under my white fur, my skin is black.
My fur is actually see-through, not white.
I’m classed as a marine mammal.
I hunt seals from the sea ice.
My day is 27 February.
The biggest land carnivore, living in the Arctic.

pearl: Losing sea ice makes hunting seals harder, which is why polar bears are vulnerable.

title: Stone faces

clues.t: I’m one of the most remote inhabited islands on Earth.
I belong to Chile.
My statues are called moai.
Many of my statues have hidden bodies buried in the ground.
A Dutch explorer arrived on Easter Sunday in 1722.
Island of giant stone heads in the Pacific.

pearl: There are nearly 1,000 moai; the biggest standing one weighs over 80 tonnes.
